audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic: EL topics include EVM opcodes (MCOPY), state clearing (Spurious Dragon), deposit request extraction (Prague), difficulty bomb delay (Muir Glacier), no-ether transactions (EIP-7768), and Verkle witness handling (EIP-6800). CL topics include light client sync protocols (Altair, Capella), beacon chain Verkle witness validation (EIP-6800), and Fulu validator custody/blob handling.

in_scope: Execution Payload Validation with Verkle Witnesses
Validator Custody and Blob Sidecar Distribution (Fulu)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EL component: EVM execution environment is part of the Execution Layer, not an external entity. It processes transactions within the system boundary.
Internal EL component: CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes are part of the EVM instruction set, executing within the system boundary.
Internal EL component: The EVM bytecode interpreter is the core of the Execution Layer, not an external entity.
Internal EL component: The deposit contract exists within the EL state trie. Its logs are read internally during block processing, not received from outside the system.
Misnamed: When viewed from EL, the CL communicates via Engine API. Should be modeled as 'CL via Engine API' with SEMI_TRUSTED level. Refined below.

trusted_external_entities.name: Full Node via P2P Network (Light Client Server)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip / Beacon API light client endpoints
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Full nodes providing light client updates, bootstraps, and headers are untrusted peers on the P2P network. Any node can serve fabricated data. The light client protocol relies on cryptographic verification (BLS aggregate signatures, Merkle proofs) to validate data from these untrusted sources.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Light Client Server
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip / Beacon API (LightClientUpdate, LightClientFinalityUpdate, LightClientBootstrap)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any node providing light client data may be malicious or compromised. All received updates must be cryptographically verified including sync committee signatures, finality Merkle proofs, and execution payload proofs (Capella+).

trusted_external_entities.name: External Trust Source (Out-of-Band Bootstrap)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Out-of-band mechanism (social consensus, trusted website) providing initial trusted block root
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The initial trusted block root is obtained through external, unverifiable means. If compromised, the entire light client chain of trust collapses. Treated as UNTRUSTED because there is no cryptographic authentication of this channel.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via the Engine API, authenticated with JWT. The channel is authenticated but payload content (execution payloads, Verkle witnesses) must still be fully validated by the EL. The CL relays data from block proposers which may be malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (BeaconBlock with ExecutionPayload containing Verkle witness)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers submit blocks via the P2P gossip network. A malicious validator could propose blocks with invalid execution payloads or crafted Verkle witnesses. All content must be validated through the full consensus and execution verification pipeline.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Engine via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The execution engine is a locally co-deployed component communicating via authenticated Engine API (JWT). It is trusted for correct execution of state transitions and Verkle proof verification. However, a buggy or compromised EL could return incorrect results, so it is SEMI_TRUSTED.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p / libp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P network are unauthenticated and may be malicious. They can send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received data must be independently validated. Applies to both EL devp2p peers and CL libp2p peers.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer/Miner via P2P (PoW context)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network (block headers with difficulty claims)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: In PoW context (EIP-2384 Muir Glacier), miners produce blocks with stated difficulty. Block difficulty must be independently recalculated and verified against the difficulty formula. A miner could attempt to submit blocks with incorrect difficulty.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC / Proposer Service
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via JSON-RPC or proposer relay services. Transactions may be malformed, attempt resource exhaustion, or contain malicious payloads. No authentication is required for public JSON-RPC endpoints. EIP-7768 introduces zero-balance EOAs submitting via proposer services, adding further attack surface.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peers (Data Availability Sampling)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers providing column sidecar data for data availability are untrusted. They may withhold data, serve invalid columns, or misrepresent custody capabilities in their ENR. Column data must be verified against KZG commitments.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P (Archetypal)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: a malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations (triggering slashing conditions), or attempt censorship. All validator-sourced data must be validated against consensus rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: External MEV-Boost Relay (Archetypal)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: MEV-Boost relay API / External builder API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: MEV-Boost relays and external block builders are untrusted third-party services that could provide incorrect execution payloads, censor transactions, or perform denial of service. Data from relays must be independently verified.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P gossip / Beacon API light client endpoints
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All light client updates must be cryptographically verified: BLS aggregate signature verification over sync committee, Merkle branch verification for finality and execution payload proofs, slot ordering validation, and minimum participation threshold checks.

Full cryptographic verification pipeline required: sync committee signature verification, finality Merkle proof verification, execution payload Merkle proof verification (Capella+). No update should be applied without passing all validation steps.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Light client bootstrap initialization (trusted block root input)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The trusted block root MUST correspond to a canonical chain block. If this root is compromised, all subsequent light client validation is compromised. This is the root of trust for the entire light client protocol. Users must obtain this via reliable out-of-band channels.

JWT authentication validates the channel. However, execution payload content must be fully validated: parent hash consistency, RANDAO mix, timestamp alignment, blob commitment counts, transaction validity, and (post-EIP-6800) Verkle witness verification. The CL relays proposer data which may be adversarial.

Block proposer data must be validated through complete consensus validation pipeline: slot verification, proposer eligibility, execution payload validity via Engine API, and (post-EIP-6800) Verkle witness structural and cryptographic verification.

The CL trusts the EL to correctly verify execution payloads and return accurate results. JWT authenticates the channel. The CL cannot independently re-verify execution-layer state transitions. A compromised EL would compromise CL's view of execution validity.

All blocks and transactions from P2P peers must be independently validated: block header fields (difficulty, gas limit, timestamp), transaction signatures, nonce ordering, gas pricing, state transition correctness. Eclipse attack mitigations required.

Block difficulty must be independently recalculated using the difficulty formula with fork-adjusted block numbers (post-Muir Glacier: max(0, block.number - 9,000,000)). Stated difficulty in headers cannot be trusted.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce validation, gas limit checks, balance sufficiency (or zero-balance handling per EIP-7768), contract code size limits (24KB per EIP-170), and state clearing rules (EIP-161). For EIP-7768 no-ether transactions, proposer must perform double-execution verification to ensure consideration consistency.

Column sidecar data must be verified against KZG commitments from the beacon block. Peers may serve invalid columns or withhold data. Custody group assignments must be independently computed. ENR custody claims cannot be trusted without verification.

All validator messages must be validated against consensus rules. Invalid blocks must be rejected. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing detection. Proposer eligibility must be verified. No validator message should be trusted based solely on validator identity.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: MEV-Boost relay API / External builder API
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Execution payloads from external builders via MEV-Boost relays must be fully validated through the same pipeline as locally-built payloads. No trust should be placed in relay assertions about payload validity or value. Relay availability cannot be guaranteed.
